name: ISO7720DR
title: ISO7720 / ISO7721 dual-channel 100 Mbps capacitive digital isolators
summary: Two-channel digital isolators that pass CMOS or LVCMOS logic across a double capacitive SiO2 barrier at up to 100 Mbps, each side running from its own 2.25 V to 5.5 V supply, so the part also shifts logic levels. The ISO7720 has both channels running from side 1 to side 2; the ISO7721 has one channel each way. Without power or input the outputs sit high, or low on the F-suffix versions. The wide-body DW-16 and DWV-8 packages are rated 5000 VRMS for one minute and the narrow D-8 3000 VRMS; the ISO7721B carries basic insulation ratings only.
key_figures: 1.7 mA per channel typ at 1 Mbps

circuits.title: Isolated 4-mA to 20-mA current loop
circuits.description: A 3.3 V microcontroller on the supply side sends data to a 4-20 mA DAC on the isolated side through the ISO7721 in its DW-16 package. Channel B carries the microcontroller's P3.1 across to the DAC's DIN; channel A brings the DAC's DBACK readback the other way into P3.0. Power for the isolated side comes from an SN6501 push-pull driver into a 1:1.33 centre-tapped transformer, a full-wave rectifier of two MBR0520L Schottky diodes, and a TPS76333 LDO that makes 3.3 V ISO. The DAC drives an external NPN whose collector sits on LOOP+, with a 22 Ω emitter resistor to isolated ground; the DAC's OUT pin is LOOP-. Every supply pin has a 0.1 µF bypass.

parts.value: IN: 0 V without F suffix, VCC with F suffix

operation.text: Each channel uses on-off keying: for one logic state the transmitter puts a high-frequency carrier across the SiO2 capacitive barrier, for the other it sends nothing. The receiver conditions and envelope-detects the carrier and drives the output buffer. The design aims at high CMTI and low radiated emission from the carrier and the I/O switching.

ISO7720: both channels pass from side 1 to side 2. ISO7721: channel A passes from side 2 to side 1, channel B from side 1 to side 2. Each side's supply is independent, 2.25 V to 5.5 V, so a channel also translates between the two logic levels.

With its input open or its input-side supply off, a channel's output goes to the default state: high on parts without the F suffix, low on F parts. The output follows the input again once VCCI returns. tDO, the delay from VCC falling below 1.7 V to the default state, is 0.1 µs typical, 0.3 µs max, tested with a 10 mV/ns ramp. With the output-side supply off, the output is undetermined.

Each supply has UVLO: the rising threshold is 2 V typical (2.25 V max), the falling threshold 1.8 V typical (1.7 V min), with 200 mV typical hysteresis. Between 1.7 V and 2.25 V the outputs are undetermined.

Each input reaches the circuit through 985 Ω, with a 1.5 MΩ resistor to VCCI on parts without the F suffix and to ground on F parts. Each output is a CMOS buffer from VCCO with about 20 Ω of output resistance.

On-chip measures for ESD, EFT, surge and emissions: strong ESD cells on the signal pins and the bond pads between the dies, low-resistance paths from those cells to supply and ground, a sturdier high-voltage isolation capacitor, larger on-chip decoupling, guard rings between PMOS and NMOS against parasitic SCR latch, and fully differential internal signalling to keep common-mode current across the barrier low.

The channels are single-ended CMOS and suit single-ended CMOS or TTL logic lines; they follow no interface standard. The isolator usually sits between a controller (an MCU or UART) and a data converter or line transceiver such as RS-485, RS-232 or CAN. Apart from the two supply bypass capacitors the part needs no external parts.

Put a 0.1 µF bypass capacitor on VCC1 and on VCC2, as near the pins as possible. Where only one supply exists, the isolated side can be powered through a transformer driver such as the SN6501 or SN6505A.

A low-EMI board needs at least four layers, top to bottom: high-speed signals, ground plane, power plane, low-speed signals. High-speed traces on the top layer need no vias; the ground plane under them gives controlled impedance and a short return path; the adjacent power and ground planes add about 100 pF/in² of bypass capacitance; slow control lines go on the bottom. Extra layers are added as a further power and ground pair to keep the stack symmetrical and flat. The example stack is 10 mil, 40 mil and 10 mil between layers in FR-4 (εr about 4.5), with the area under the isolator kept clear of planes, traces, pads and vias.

FR-4 UL94V-0 board is specified for links under 150 Mbps (rise and fall times above 1 ns) with traces up to 10 in. Against cheaper laminates it has lower dielectric loss at high frequency, takes up less moisture, is stronger and stiffer, and is self-extinguishing.

Lifetime is projected by time-dependent dielectric breakdown testing: each side's pins shorted together, high 60 Hz voltage applied across the barrier at several levels and temperatures (oven at 150 °C), time to a current above 1 mA counted. VDE reinforced certification takes the projection line for under 1 ppm failures and adds 20% margin on voltage and 50% on life, so 30 years is required at 1.2 times the working voltage. The barrier's projected capability is 1500 VRMS for 36 years; DW-16 and DWV-8 are specified to 1500 VRMS working voltage and D-8 to 450 VRMS, with longer life at lower voltage. Package size, pollution degree and material group can set a lower working voltage.
At 100 Mbps PRBS with 5 V supplies at 25 °C, both ISO7720 and ISO7721 show a wide open eye with low jitter (1 V/div, 3.5 ns/div).
AEC-Q100 qualified versions are the ISO7720-Q1 and ISO7721-Q1.
